commits.message:
feat(auth): enforce tenant scope and RBAC on sensitive routes

Phase 6 of the auth integration: the routers now derive their tenant from the
authenticated principal and name the permission they require, instead of
trusting a company UUID supplied by the caller.

deps.py gains `PathCompanyId`. Many routes were written with the company in the
URL, which reads naturally but let any authenticated caller substitute another
tenant's UUID. The dependency compares the path parameter against the
principal's company and answers 403 on mismatch, so the URL shape and the
OpenAPI schema stay as they were.

Cross-tenant holes closed:

* api_keys.py — any authenticated user could mint or list keys for any company,
  and revoke or delete any key by id. Now administrator-only, with the company
  predicate inside the UPDATE and DELETE so a foreign id reads as 404 rather
  than confirming it exists. Keys may also be issued with a role of their own.
* companies.py — `list_companies` returned every company on the platform; the
  id routes accepted any UUID. Listing is now scoped by membership, and
  creating a company grants the creator membership of it so the new tenant is
  reachable.
* budgets.py, evolution.py, profile.py — `{company_id}` validated against the
  principal.
* profile.py — looked its subject up by company and took whichever row came
  back, so in a company with more than one member every caller read and wrote a
  colleague's profile; with an empty table it fabricated `admin@nvlabs.company`
  and returned it as fact. Now scoped to `principal.user_id`.

Permission guards: write on policy, incident and evolution; approve on
evolution proposals (which admits managers, whose role already carries the
approval duty); read on the policy and proposal evaluators, which compute
rather than mutate.

Removed from profile.py, because working versions live in auth.py which owns
the session table:

* `change-password`, which verified nothing and returned `{"success": true}`
  without touching the database;
* three session endpoints scoped by *company* that issued hard DELETEs against
  `user_sessions` — the table the login cookie resolves through — letting any
  member sign out everyone in the company;
* the two-factor switch, which flipped a flag no login path checks. The column
  stays; the switch returns with the TOTP verification that makes it mean
  something.

Also fixed while in these files: `cost_trend` and two evolution handlers called
`datetime.now(timezone.utc)` without importing `timezone`, so they raised
NameError on every request. The evolution pair sat in a duplicate block that
redefined three handlers already defined above it — dead code, since FastAPI
routes the first registration, and now deleted.

The SSE and WebSocket auth tests asserted the old header contract (400 without
`X-Company-Id`). They now assert the real one: 401 for an anonymous request,
and a self-asserted company header authenticates nothing.

Suite: 3050 passed, 13 failed, all thirteen pre-existing on HEAD (which fails
16, including the three stale SSE tests this commit rewrites).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.message:
feat(auth): add auth routes, first-run setup, and bootstrap command

Adds the HTTP surface for the auth system: login, logout, session
listing and revocation, company switching, password change, invites,
and a one-shot first-run setup endpoint that only answers while the
user table is empty.

fastapi-users routers are deliberately not mounted. Only
BaseUserManager.authenticate and the password helper are used;
onboarding is invite-only and there is no mailer, so a reset endpoint
could only hand a reset token to whoever asked for it.

nexus.auth.bootstrap is the lockout-recovery path the setup endpoint
cannot be: it creates or repairs an administrator from the command
line, resetting the password and restoring is_active for an account
that already exists.

pick_setup_company is shared by both so the CLI and the endpoint land
in the same tenant as the seeded development company.

commits.message:
feat(auth): add auth core (principal, sessions, API keys, CSRF, middleware)

Adds the request-authentication layer that later phases build on.

Principal is the single resolved identity for a request: either a human
(cookie session) or a service (API key), always scoped to exactly one
company and carrying one role. Routes never see a raw header again.

AuthenticationMiddleware is ASGI middleware rather than a FastAPI
dependency because GovernanceMiddleware runs before any route dependency
resolves; the kill switch, policy evaluation and budget pre-check would
otherwise still key off a client-supplied company header. The middleware
never rejects an anonymous request -- it only annotates the scope -- so
authorization stays a per-route decision. Its two rejections are a failed
CSRF double-submit check and a WebSocket handshake from an unlisted
origin; the latter matters because browsers send no preflight for
WebSockets, so the CORS middleware cannot police them.

Session and invite tokens are stored as SHA-256 hashes only, and a null
expiry is treated as expired rather than eternal. Cookie sessions
re-check company membership on every request so revoking access takes
effect immediately instead of when the cookie happens to lapse.

rbac.py gains permission_grants and role_allows so the same role
vocabulary drives both the existing RBACManager and the new middleware.

api_key.py and auth.py now take their timestamp default from
nexus.models._time.utcnow, matching the naive TIMESTAMP columns the rest
of the schema uses.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
commits.author: Navi

commits.message:
feat(auth): add auth schema, settings, and migration

Phase 1 of integrating fastapi-users. Schema and configuration only; no
behaviour changes yet, since nothing reads these columns until the auth
middleware lands.

Dependencies: replace the declared-but-unimported python-jose and passlib
with fastapi-users[sqlalchemy]>=15.0.5. That brings pwdlib[argon2,bcrypt]
for hashing and pyjwt for token signing, and via
fastapi-users-db-sqlalchemy it introduces an upper bound of
sqlalchemy[asyncio]<2.1.0.

Models: UserProfile becomes the fastapi-users user table directly. SQLModel
classes are SQLAlchemy declarative models, so SQLAlchemyUserDatabase accepts
UserProfile once it carries email, hashed_password, is_active, is_superuser
and is_verified — no second user table and no shared-metadata shim.
UserSession gains a uniquely indexed token_hash plus expires_at and
revoked_at, so a session cookie is an opaque random token whose SHA-256 is
all the database ever holds. ApiKey gains a role, letting a service key be
issued with less authority than its creator, and created_by for provenance.

Authorization reuses the existing company_memberships table rather than
adding a parallel one; nothing but a model test referenced it. Because its
role column defaulted to "member", which is not an RBAC role,
normalize_role() resolves unrecognised values to "viewer". auth.py adds only
the invite table, since onboarding is invite-only.

A new models/_time.utcnow() returns naive UTC. Every datetime column in this
package is a naive TIMESTAMP (no model declares timezone=True); asyncpg
rejects an aware value for such a column, and comparing an aware value
against one loaded from the database raises TypeError, which would have
broken session-expiry checks on every request.

Migration dedupes user_profiles.email before making its index unique. The
old GET /api/v1/profile fabricated a profile per company, all using
admin@nvlabs.company, so multi-company databases hold duplicates; each one
after the first is rewritten to dup+<id>@invalid.local rather than deleted,
since user_sessions references those rows. Verified upgrade and downgrade
round-trip against a seeded SQLite database containing exact and
case-variant duplicates.

Config: auth_enabled, cookie names, session lifetime and password floor,
with validator warnings for a wildcard CORS origin (illegal alongside
credentialed cookies), a default secret key, disabled auth, and insecure
session cookies.

Tests: test_alembic_migration expected 56 tables. Committing api_key.py and
user_profile.py (previously untracked) plus the new auth_invites table makes
that 60, so EXPECTED_TABLES and both count assertions are updated.

models/__init__.py imports only tracked modules. The working tree also holds
uncommitted notification.py, pipeline.py, repository.py and settings.py; their
import lines are left out so a fresh checkout can import nexus.models.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.message:
docs: add auth design spec for fastapi-users integration

Design for adding authentication and tenant identity to NEXUS. Today
X-Company-Id is trusted verbatim at deps.py:20 and middleware.py:101,
so any client can select any tenant and also choose which company's
kill switch, policy set, and budget it is measured against.

Approach: fastapi-users 15.0.5 as a library, with an
AuthenticationMiddleware wrapping GovernanceMiddleware so the principal
is resolved before the governance gates run. CurrentCompanyId keeps its
name and type, sourced from the principal, leaving all 35 routers
unchanged.

Covers the data model (users, company_memberships, api_keys,
company_invites, plus repurposed user_sessions/user_profiles),
principal resolution, module layout, endpoints, role guards on eight
sensitive route files, frontend cookie migration, error semantics,
CSRF/CORS/CSWSH handling, test fixtures, and a four-commit rollout
behind AUTH_ENABLED.
